proposed_english: the ⲡⲱⲧ (organ — possibly lung or dorsal organ)
rationale: First of three internal organs listed in the third cosmos before liver and bile. Standard Manichaean visceral inventory suggests heart/lung/spleen/liver/gall/kidneys; since heart belongs to the 2nd cosmos here, ⲡⲱⲧ is likely 'lungs' or another dorsal/upper-abdominal organ. Etymology unclear; possibly cognate with ⲡⲱⲧ 'back, dorsum.'

Second internal organ in third cosmos. Literally 'the flesh' (ⲟⲩⲁϥ = Sah. ⲟⲩⲱϥ 'meat, flesh'). May designate a specific fleshy abdominal organ — possibly the diaphragm or a muscle-mass — within the visceral schema.

Third internal organ in third cosmos, between ⲡⲟⲩⲁϥ and ⲡⲍⲏⲡⲁⲣ (liver). By position in the visceral list and dialect-pattern matching, possibly 'spleen' (Sah. ⲗⲟⲩⲗ?) or another major abdominal organ. Confidence low.

In the body-cosmos correspondence schema, the two arms of the 2nd cosmos correspond to two ⲙⲉϣⲧⲉ in the 1st cosmos (head). Since the head's pairs are eyes/ears/nostrils, and ⲙⲁⲛϣⲱⲗⲙⲉ 'nostrils' and ⲙⲁⲛⲓⲱⲣⲍ 'eyes' are accounted for elsewhere on the page, ⲙⲉϣⲧⲉ here = 'ear' (Lyc. variant of ⲙⲁⲁϫⲉ/ⲙⲁⲥϫⲉ).

Lyc. ⲃⲉⲗ = ⲃⲁⲗ 'eye, opening.' In cardiac context likely refers to the chambers (atria/ventricles) — i.e., the heart's 'eyes' or 'orifices.' Used here in dual ⲥⲛⲉⲩ as a paired feature within the second cosmos schema. Preserves correspondential register: the cardiac orifices ARE eyes in the body-cosmos mapping.

The substance that 'comes forth from the (genital) member' and 'begets all the forms.' Clearly = semen/seed in correspondential register. Etymology uncertain; possibly Lyc. for ⲥⲡⲟⲣⲟⲥ/ⲥⲡⲉⲣⲙⲁ or a native generative-noun.

The lower limit of the second cosmos, defined as extending 'from the neck downward as far as his entire ϣⲁϣⲡⲉ.' Anatomically must be navel or lower-trunk boundary. Possibly Lyc. variant of ϩⲉⲗⲡⲉ 'navel' or related to ϣⲁϣⲧⲉ 'shaft.' Confidence low.
First of three paired leg-parts in the 4th (lower) cosmos: ⲧⲉⲧⲉ ⲥⲛⲉⲩ + ⲭⲁⲓ̈ⲧ ⲥⲛⲉⲩ + ⲕⲉⲍⲧⲉ ⲥⲛ̄ⲧⲉ (thighs). By anatomical position likely 'buttocks' or 'hips.' Confidence low.
Second of three paired leg-parts in the 4th cosmos. Distinct from ⲕⲉⲍⲧⲉ 'thighs.' Likely a lower-leg or pelvic part. Confidence low.

In the construction ⲁⲩⲉⲉⲩ ⲛ̄ⲭⲱⲭ 'they made them into a ⲭⲱⲭ' applied to the twelve zodiac signs in the celestial wheel. Possibly Lyc. for ϫⲱⲱϫⲉ 'row, course' or related. Fits zodiacal-rotation imagery.

Recurs twice in line 30-31 in construction ⲁⲧⲣⲉⲕⲟ̄ⲛ ⲧⲁⲡⲉ ⲛ̄[X] ⲛ̄ⲕⲟ̄ⲛ. Possibly Greek κανών 'rule, canon,' κῶνος 'cone,' or Coptic ⲕⲱⲛ 'embrace, lap.' Cosmic-administrative sense (rule/canon) fits zodiac-governance context. Flagged for parallels.

Possibly Lyc. contraction of ⲥⲉⲧⲉ 'fire' (cf. ⲡⲭⲁⲓ̈ ⲛⲧⲥⲉⲧⲉ 'sun-ship'). Alternative readings: ⲥⲛⲧⲉ 'foundation,' ⲥⲏⲧ 'tail.' Context (cosmic-elemental enumeration alongside the wheel of stars) admits 'fire' as a parallel cosmic principle. Confidence low.
